notes:
Overview: Sablecliff is a product analytics SaaS aiming to add an in-app assistant plus semantic search and a reranking layer to improve discovery and reduce support load. They want to prototype on Hosted API for rapid iteration and then evaluate Dedicated if cost and latency targets are met.

Workload specifics:
- Mix: multi-turn chat for helpdesk, embeddings for search (1-2k docs per request for vector retrieval), reranking on top-20 candidates. Typical reply token size ~280-400.
- Performance targets: p95 chat latency < 350ms under normal load; embeddings p50 < 120ms.
- Scale: target steady-state 300-500 QPS, peaks to 900 QPS for release days.
- Cost sensitivity: high. Finance requires a 12-month TCO comparison and a clear break-even point for switching to Dedicated.

Cost workshop 02/26 - highlights:
- Facilitator: Priya Nair. Ran through batching windows, adaptive batch sizing, prefix KV caching, and quantization tradeoffs.
- Recommendations: use adaptive batching with 30ms baseline window plus dynamic upsizing for burst traffic; implement route-based caching (homepage onboarding prompts) to capture repeated prefixes; evaluate int8 and gptq profiles for reranker model (expected 1.4-1.8x cost reduction depending on quality SLA).
- Experiment plan: run three POC branches: (A) hosted baseline, (B) hosted + batching/caching, (C) Dedicated sizing w/ quantized models. Each branch to run on 100k synthetic sessions to compare token savings and latency.
- Unit economics: built scenario table showing Hosted per-token costs vs 12-mo Dedicated commit at two sizes. Example: 150M tokens/mo => hosted est $9.5k/mo, Dedicated amortized $5.8k/mo (with reserved nodes + 10% autoscale). Spreadsheet linked in Drive.
- Ops playbook: recommended fallback routing policy to default small-model variant during capacity pressure, and a cache warming strategy prior to marketing spikes.

POC technical notes:
- Baseline hosted test: avg tokens/session 460, cost/session $0.0118, p50 latency 170ms, p95 latency 390ms.
- After enabling adaptive batching (30ms) + KV prefix cache sample: token reductions ~24% for support flows, p50 latency increase +25ms. Quality checks show no meaningful regression on rerank NDCG@10.
- Quantization trials: gptq int8 gave 1.5x throughput improvement on reranker hardware; need to validate model-quality in A/B against human eval set.

Security and compliance:
- Must have SSO (SAML), SOC2 Type II, audit log retention 12 months, KMS key wrapping and EU data residency for EU customers. Legal flagged contractual language for data processing addendum.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- "We need a defensible number: if batching + cache gets us over 20% token savings, Dedicated justification is straightforward." 1@Head of Product (Lena Ortiz) during cost lab.
- "Procurement needs a vendor SOC2 and a sample SIEM log output by 2026-03-22." 1@Legal (Markus Kim).
